SMTO-WEB-0008 — That web address keeps sending SMTO somewhere else

GUID: b2318fc0-7288-46f4-aa03-7e8976743122
Slug: web-too-many-redirects
Domain: WEB · Subsystem: web

What happened

  • When SMTO opened the address, the site sent it on to another address more than five times in a row, so SMTO stopped following. Nothing was read.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the same address in your web browser, wait for the page to load, then copy the address shown in the address bar. Your browser follows the redirects and shows the page's final address.
  2. Give that final address to SMTO in the conversation and ask it to read that page. Starting at the final address avoids the long chain of redirects.
  3. If your browser also can't load it or says the page redirects too many times, ask SMTO to use a different source. The site is then stuck in a redirect loop, which only its owner can fix.

What success looks like

  • SMTO reads the page from the final address and shows its content.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the address, to the person who manages SMTO, or tell the website's owner about the redirect loop. Don't ask anyone to raise or remove SMTO's redirect limit.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Web reader stopped because the page redirected again after the maximum of five redirects.

What this means

  • The reader encounters another redirect after its maximum permitted redirect count. The diagnostic adds no retrieval. Read outcomes and retained receipts determine what evidence is available; an error does not establish the content of an unread source.

Why this can happen

  • The reader encounters another redirect after its maximum permitted redirect count.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the recorded redirect chain for loops or an unintended endpoint.

How to fix it

  • read_page in src/agent_runtime/skills/web/reader.py follows at most MAX_REDIRECTS (5) 3xx responses, re-validating public DNS at each hop; inspect the recorded redirects list for a loop or long chain. Use the final intended URL or have the site fix its redirect configuration; do not bypass redirect validation.
  • Use the final intended URL or correct the server redirect loop.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended final public URL is reached within the supported redirect bound.

What not to do

  • Do not bypass redirect validation or the redirect limit to follow an unchecked destination.

Technical notes

  • The diagnostic adds no retrieval. Read outcomes and retained receipts determine what evidence is available; an error does not establish the content of an unread source.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
